title: Puerto Rico Senate Hears Water, Power, and Tourism Agencies Oppose Esencia Megaproject Bad Bunny Targeted Onstage
detail: The Puerto Rico Senate's Commission on Innovation, Reform and Appointments, chaired by Senate President Thomas Rivera Schatz, held a public hearing under Senate Resolutions 9 and 459 investigating the feasibility of the roughly $2 billion Proyecto Esencia tourism-residential megaproject in Cabo Rojo's Los Pozos sector — the same project Bad Bunny demanded be "canceled" from the Hiram Bithorn stage on his Aug. 22–23 tour-closing nights, and that thousands marched against in Cabo Rojo on Aug. 23 following his on-screen call to action. Three government agencies testified against the project as proposed: the Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (AAA) said existing infrastructure cannot supply the project's roughly 1.25 million gallons of daily groundwater demand; the Electric Power Authority (AEE) said the regional system already operates at capacity and recommended alternatives like seawater desalination; and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company (CTPR) said the project is predominantly residential rather than tourism-focused and recommended scaling back its residential footprint. Senator Eliezer Molina said it was the first time in his career he had seen the Office of Permit Management (OGPe) grant permits over the unanimous opposition of government agencies. The Senate president said he would not allow flawed permitting processes to proceed without proper legal review.
